title: Keyboard-first aggregation and accessible live-tooltip for dense time-series
creator: Anika Shah
description: Problem: High-density time-series used in monitoring dashboards creates crowded hover areas and a noisy tooltip experience. Keyboard users and screen-reader users cannot reliably inspect aggregated values for dense clusters. CPU-bound rendering of every point on hover also spikes on pages with many series. Goal: Design an interaction and visual treatment that provides clear, keyboard-navigable aggregation of clustered data, an accessible live-tooltip pattern (ARIA-friendly), and recommendations for graceful performance degradation (progressive decimation + canvas fallback). This ticket covers the design spec, accessibility requirements, and interaction states to hand off to engineering and QA.
acceptance_criteria: Keyboard navigation: users can tab into a chart focus region and use arrow keys to move between logical x-axis aggregations (not every pixel).
Aggregation snap: when focused on a dense region, tooltip shows aggregated summary (min/median/max/count) and an affordance to expand into series-level drilldown.
ARIA: a single live region announces aggregation summaries on focus change; focus order is predictable and documented.
Performance guidance: design includes a visual 'summary layer' that can be rendered as lightweight SVG or canvas; spec includes fallback styles for <50ms hover update goal on typical pages.
Edge cases: behavior defined for sparse vs dense series, high series count (>20), and streaming updates (new points).
Design handoff: Figma frames, tokens, and interaction prototypes delivered; acceptance verified in a11y audit and perf checklist (see design_links).
updates: 2026-03-14 — Synced with ENG infra team. Agreed to expose a chart-level 'interaction-mode' flag to toggle between full-point focus and aggregated focus. Outcome: we will ship aggregated mode by default for >= 8 series. Marco to add implementation notes.

2026-03-10 — Initial exploratory sketches completed. Two patterns tested: (A) aggregation overlay with inline expand button; (B) keyboard navigator that steps by bucket. Usability review preferred pattern A for mobile, pattern B for keyboard-heavy flows. Decided to combine patterns: aggregation overlay + keyboard bucket stepping.

2026-03-05 — Accessibility review with Sari (a11y specialist). Recommended single aria-live region and avoiding redundant announcement of unchanged values when streaming. Also called out need for high-contrast borders for the focus ring; token names added to tokens backlog.
2026-03-02 — Ticket created. Problem statement and initial goals logged. Assigned to Marco for prototyping; estimate 3 points.
decisions: Use aggregation-by-bucket for dense clusters rather than attempting to surface every point to keyboard users.
Expose a compact summary in the primary tooltip: count, min, median, max, and a small sparkline of the bucket.
Provide a dedicated keyboard 'expand' action (Enter) to reveal series-level list in a panel instead of trying to render dozens of inline tooltips.
Implement aria-live="polite" (documented) for non-disruptive announcements and avoid flashing announcements when values do not change.
tradeoffs: Aggregation improves accessibility and performance but loses per-point immediacy — mitigated by explicit expand-to-drilldown affordance.
Canvas-based decimation delivers best perf on large payloads but reduces DOM-level semantics; we pair canvas rendering with an offscreen accessible representation for screen readers.
Defaulting to aggregated mode at >=8 series simplifies UX for most dashboards but may require an override for power users — add a control in chart settings.
